LEGENDRIAN CONE STRUCTURES AND CONTACT
PROLONGATIONS
JUN-MUK HWANG
Abstract. We study a cone structure C ⊂PD on a holomorphic con-
tact manifold (M, D ⊂TM) such that each ﬁber Cx ⊂PDx is isomorphic
to a Legendrian submanifold of ﬁxed isomorphism type. By character-
izing subadjoint varieties among Legendrian submanifold in terms of
contact prolongations, we prove that the canonical distribution on the
associated contact G-structure admits a holomorphic horizontal split-
ting.
MSC 2010. 53B99, 14J45
Keywords. contact structure, prolongation, Legendrian submanifold, G-
structure
1. Introduction
We will work in the complex analytic setting: all geometric objects refer
to holomorphic ones.
A contact structure on a complex manifold M of dimension 2n + 1 is a
subbundle D ⊂TM of rank 2n such that the Lie bracket of vector ﬁelds
induces a nondegenerate bilinear form
ωx : ∧2Dx →Lx
for each x ∈M, where L is the quotient line bundle TM/D. The following
conjecture is well-known.
Conjecture 1.1. Let X be a Fano manifold with a contact structure D ⊂
TX. Assume that PicX ∼= Z · L for the line bundle L = TX/D. Then X is
homogeneous.
Conjecture 1.1 has drawn much attention because it implies the LeBrun-
Salamon conjecture on quaternion-K¨ahler manifolds in Riemannian holo-
nomy theory, for which we may assume additionally that X is K¨ahler-
Einstein (see [Le]).
One approach to Conjecture 1.1 is via contact lines and their varieties of
minimal rational tangents. To explain this approach, we recall the following
deﬁnitions.
Deﬁnition 1.2. Let (V, σ) be a symplectic vector space, i.e., a vector space
V equipped with a symplectic form σ : ∧2V →C.
(1) The conformal symplectic group CSp(V ) ⊂GL(V ) is the direct sum
of the symplectic group Sp(V ) and the center C× · IdV .

(2) A projective subvariety Z ⊂PV is Legendrian if its aﬃne cone bZ ⊂V
satisﬁes dim bZ = 1
2 dim V and is isotropic with respect to σ, i.e.,
ω(T bZ,v, T bZ,v) = 0
for each nonsingular point v ∈bZ. Here, we regard the tangent space
T bZ,z as a subspace of V . We say that Z is a Legendrian submanifold
if furthermore it is nonsingular.
(3) A Legendrian submanifold Z ⊂PV is nondegenerate if the aﬃne
cone bZ ⊂V spans the vector space V .
(4) A nondegenerate Legendrian submanifold Z ⊂PV is a subadjoint
variety if the group GZ ⊂CSp(V ) of elements of CSp(V ) preserving
bZ ⊂V acts transitively on Z.
The above deﬁnition of subadjoint varieties agrees with the standard one
by Theorem 11 of [LM]. Many examples of Legendrian submanifolds in PV
other than subadjoint varieties are given in [Bu07], [Bu08] and [LM].
In the setting of Conjecture 1.1, a rational curve C ⊂X is called a contact
line if C · L = 1 and C is tangent to D ⊂TX. It is known that contact lines
exist through every point of X.
Kebekus proved the following result in
Theorem 4.1 and Theorem 4.4 of [Ke2].
Theorem 1.3. For X, D and L as in Conjecture 1.1, ﬁx an irreducible
component K of the space of contact lines such that members of K cover X.
Let x ∈X be a general point and Kx ⊂K be the subscheme parametrizing
members of K passing through x. Then
(a) all members of Kx are nonsingular;
(b) the algebraic subset Cx ⊂PDx consisting of tangent spaces to mem-
bers of Kx is nonsingular; and
(c) each irreducible component of Cx is a Legendrian submanifold for the
symplectic form ωx on Dx.
The subset Cx ⊂PDx in Theorem 1.3 is precisely the variety of minimal
rational tangents of the Fano manifold X in the sense of [HM98] or [H01]. By
applying the theory of varieties of minimal rational tangents, Mok obtained
the following result (Main Theorem in Section 2 of [Mo]).
Theorem 1.4. In the setting of Theorem 1.3, if Cx is a subadjoint variety,
then X is homogeneous.
This seems to be a promising approach to Conjecture 1.1, as it does not
assume the existence of vector ﬁelds on X. However, no good strategy has
been suggested so far to prove Cx is a subadjoint variety in Theorem 1.3.
This gives a motivation to study the geometry of general ‘Legendrian cone
structure’ in the following sense.
Deﬁnition 1.5. Let D ⊂TM be a contact structure on a complex manifold
M and let ωx : ∧2Dx →Lx be the associated symplectic form at each

x ∈M. A submanifold C ⊂PD is a Legendrian cone structure on M if each
ﬁber Cx ⊂PDx is a Legendrian submanifold in the sense of Deﬁnition 1.2.
A Legendrian cone structure is nondegenerate if Cx is nondegenerate. For
a ﬁxed Legendrian submanifold Z ⊂PV in the sense of Deﬁnition 1.2, a
Legendrian cone structure C ⊂PD on M is Z-isotrivial if the submanifold
Cx ⊂PDx is equivalent to Z ⊂PV modulo CSp(V ) for each x ∈M.
A theory of general Legendrian cone structures is yet to be developed. It
seems reasonable to start with studying Z-isotrivial Legendrian cone struc-
tures for a general nondegenerate Z ⊂PV . When Z ⊂PV is a subadjoint
variety, a Z-isotrivial Legendrian cone structure is a parabolic contact struc-
ture in the sense of Section 4.2 of [CS]. In fact, the proof of Theorem uses
the result of [Ho] which employed Tanaka connections for parabolic contact
structures. As a ﬁrst step toward the geometry of Z-isotrial Legendrian cone
structures, one may ask whether there is an analog of Tanaka connection
in this general setting. We prove the following Theorem, which says that
the canonical distribution on the associated contact G-structure admits a
holomorphic horizontal splitting. This can be viewed as an analog of Tanaka
connection.
Theorem 1.6. Let Z ⊂PV be a nondegenerate Legendrian submanifold for
a symplectic vector space (V, σ), which is not a subadjoint variety and let
G ⊂CSp(V ) the automorphism group of Z. Let M be a complex manifold
dim M = dim V + 1 equipped with a contact structure D ⊂TM and a Z-
isotrival Legendrian cone structure C ⊂PD. We have the associated G-
principal ﬁber subbundle π : P →M of the contact frame bundle of M. Let
T π ⊂TP be the kernel of dπ and let D ⊂TP be the natural distribution
satisfying D/T π ∼= π∗D. Then there exists a subbundle H ⊂D such that
D ∼= T π ⊕H.
Theorem 1.6 is an immediate consequence of two results, Theorem 2.3
and Theorem 3.1 below.
Theorem 2.3 is a general result on contact G-
structures and contact prolongations. In principle, Theorem 2.3 is contained
in Morimoto’s general theory ([Mr]) of G-structures on ﬁltered manifolds.
As it can be stated and proved more explicitly in the contact setting, we
present a self-contained account here. Theorem 3.1 is a characterization of
subadjoint varieties in terms of contact prolongations, a contact analog of
Theorem 7.13 in [FH18]. Its proof is simpler than that of [FH18], thanks to
the work [LM]. These theorems are expected to be useful in the approach
to Conjecture 1.1 via varieties of minimal rational tangents of contact lines.
2. Contact prolongation and contact G-structure
In this section, we look at the theory of contact G-structures. We will give
a self-contained presentation, modifying the ordinary G-structure theory
presented in [St]. Although this is a special case of the general theory of
geometric structures on ﬁltered manifolds developed by Morimoto in [Mo],
the explicit presentation here could be useful in applications.

3. Contact prolongation and Legendrian submanifolds
Let (V, σ) be a symplectic vector space. For a Legendrian submanifold
Z ⊂PV, let GZ ⊂CSp(V ) be the subgroup in Deﬁnition 1.2 and let gZ ⊂
csp(V ) be its Lie algebra. The main result of this section is the following.
Theorem 3.1. A nondegenerate Legendrian submanifold Z ⊂PV is a sub-
adjoint variety if gZ ⊂csp(V ) has a nonzero contact prolongation.


10
JUN-MUK HWANG
The converse of Theorem 3.1 holds, although we do not need it. One can
see it from the fact that Z-isotrivial Legendrian cone structures are parabolic
contact structures and the latter has prolongations (Section 4.2 of [CS]). To
prove Theorem 3.1, it is convenient to use the following notion from [FH17].
Deﬁnition 3.2. Let V be a vector space. A subvariety Z ⊂PV is Euler-
symmetric if for a general point z ∈Z, there exists a C×-subgroup Ez ⊂
GL(V ) such that Ez preserves Z with an isolated ﬁxed point at z and acts
trivially on PTZ,z.
The following result is Proposition 2.7 in [FH17]. We refer the reader to
[FH17] for the deﬁnition of fundamental forms of projective varieties.
Proposition 3.3. Let Z1 and Z2 be two Euler-symmetric subvarieties of
PV of equal dimension. Let z1 ∈Z1 and z2 ∈Z2 be general points. If the
systems of fundamental forms of Z1 at z1 and Z2 at z2 are isomorphic, then
Z1 and Z2 are isomorphic by a projective transformation of PV .
To apply this to Legendrian submanifolds, we recall some basic properties
of fundamental forms of Legendrian submanifolds. The following is proved
in pp. 348-349 of [LM]. Recall that for a cubic form P ∈Sym3 W ∨on a
vector space W, its Hessian is the homomorphism Sym2 W →W ∨deﬁned
by

Proposition 3.5. Let (V, σ) be a symplectic vector space.
Let Z ⊂PV
be a nondegenerate Legendrian submanifold. Then an element A ∈GL(V )
preserving bZ ⊂V belongs to CSp(V ).
Proof. To prove the proposition, it suﬃces to show that if σ′ is a symplectic
form on V with respect to which Z is Legendrian, then σ′ ∈C · σ.
Suppose that σ′ ̸∈Cσ. Then there exists a linear combination τ := σ′+c·σ
for some c ∈C such that its null space
Nullτ := {v ∈V, τ(v, u) = 0 for all u ∈V }
is nonzero. By Proposition 3.4 (2), for a general z ∈Z, we have z⊥σ = z⊥σ′.

ισ : PV →PV ∨given by z 7→Pz⊥σ sends Z into the linear subspace
annihilating Nullτ.
This is a contradiction to the assumption that Z is
nondegenerate.

Proposition 3.5 says that when we apply results like Proposition 3.3 to
nondegenerate Legendrian submanifolds, we do not need to check whether
isomorphisms as projective subvarieties respect the underlying symplectic
form on the vector space: they always do.
Proposition 3.6. For a symplectic vector space (V, σ), if a nondegenerate
Legendrian submanifold Z ⊂PV is Euler-symmetric, then it is a subadjoint
variety.
Proof. When dim V = 2n+2, for each nondegenerate cubic polynomial P in
n variables, a special Legendrian subvariety eZP ⊂P2n+1 whose third funda-
mental form at a general point is isomorphic to P is constructed in p. 357 of
[LM]. Their construction implies that eZP is Euler-symmetric. (In fact, this
is a special case of a more general construction of Euler symmetric varieties
in Deﬁnition 3.6 of [FH17], as mentioned in Example 3.10 of [FH17].) By
Proposition 3.4 (3), the system of fundamental forms of a nondegenerate
Legendrian submanifold is determined by its third fundamental form. Thus
by Proposition 3.3, an Euler-symmetric Legendrian submanifold Z ⊂PV is
projectively isomorphic to eZP ⊂P2n+1. Then by Corollary 26 of [LM], it is
a subadjoint variety.
□

Proposition 3.8. Let Z ⊂PV be a nondegenerate Legendrian submani-
fold. If gZ ⊂csp(V ) has a nonzero contact prolongation, then Z is Euler-
symmetric.
Proof. Pick a nonzero contact prolongation A of gZ.
First, assume that
⃗A = 0. Then we have Au(v) = Av(u) for all u, v ∈V . This means A is
the usual prolongation of the Lie algebra gZ ⊂gl(V ), in the sense of the
section (1.1) of [HM05] or Deﬁnition 7.9 of [FH18]. Moreover, Proposition
3.7 shows Av(v) = 0 for all v ∈bZ. This implies A = 0 by Lemma 2.2.1 of
[HM05], a contradiction.

on the tangent space of Z at the point z ∈Z corresponding to v,
TZ,z = Hom(Cv, T bZ,v/Cv),
as the identity by Proposition 3.7 (ii). In particular, the semi-simple part

Thus the C×-subgroup
